requested_parts: New invaders in already due land
entire_original_entry.answer: Determine eligibility anew before each card. The initially empty land qualifies for the second card if then occupied and matching. Invaders newly moved into a land already due participate in its Ravage.

evidence.text: Before resolving the actions from a card, determine which lands qualify; players choose the order of those lands. Changes during the card do not add newly eligible lands to that list. Determine eligibility anew for each later card, so a land newly occupied during an earlier Ravage card can Ravage under a later matching Ravage card. In a land already due to Ravage, newly arrived Invaders participate when its Ravage resolves. Resolve each land fully, including cascades and triggered effects, and check outcomes before proceeding to the next. [CORE pp.9–10; FAQ pieces-added-or-moved-by-ravages-do-not-cause-more-ravages; .9v5kaam]

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Ravages if eligible when second card checked.

entire_original_entry.answer: Invader Phase: Blighted Island, Fear, Ravage, Build, Explore, advance cards. If the start-of-phase Blighted instruction destroys last Presence, finish that action and its triggers then check defeat before proceeding to Fear; Fear cannot avert it afterward.

evidence.text: 1. **Blighted Island:** If the Blight Card is Blighted, follow its instructions at the specified timing (typically start of each Invader Phase). No such step applies with the printed no-card pool.

2. **Fear:** Turn the earned face-down stack over and resolve its cards **in the order earned**, one at a time, without looking ahead. Use **only the current Terror Level's effect**, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Discard each resolved card to Fear discard. Fear earned during this step can earn more cards: append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step. Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level. Fear earned later, such as in Ravage or Slow, waits for the next Fear step.
6. **Advance cards:** Discard the old Ravage card; slide Build to Ravage and the just-revealed Explore card to Build.

requested_parts: Initial piece placement and Blight source
entire_original_entry.answer: Use one randomly chosen balanced Island Board per Spirit and join them in a fitting balanced layout. Populate each land’s printed Invader, Dahan, and Blight icons; setup Blight comes from the box and does not cascade or destroy Presence. Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard, and make Invaders, Dahan, and Energy available to everyone.

evidence.text: 1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Choose randomly; any fitting arrangement is legal.

entire_original_entry.answer: If target has Explorers, Push all of them. If none, remove one Blight. The Blight branch is not optional when Explorers are present.

evidence.text: - **Core Power specifics:** **Song of Sanctity** is Slow, despite missing cost-circle ink in some printings. Its Explorer condition selects its effect: with Explorers, Push all of them; otherwise remove 1 Blight. This is not a free choice to remove Blight while Explorers remain. **Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship** line 3 Pushes all Explorers **to as many different lands as possible**, using every available legal destination up to the number of Explorers; its Invaders damaging each other do so simultaneously, **before** the Explorer Push as the threshold specifies. **Poisoned Land**'s threshold counts the Blight that its own earlier instruction added. **Tsunami**'s threshold adds Fear for each other Coastal land it affects. [Core: .7w4g9dg, .9v5kc31, .7w4ganc, .7w4g8q3, .7w4g8pc]

requested_parts: Bringer separate Power 2 then 1 Damage on undamaged City
two Damage instructions within one Power
entire_original_entry.answer: Separate Powers cannot combine Bringer’s hypothetical Damage: 2 Damage and then separate 1 Damage do not destroy the undamaged City or earn Fear. If 2 then 1 are instructions within one Power, they can combine to hypothetically destroy it, earning 5 Fear and pushing it. A Repeat can pretend-destroy the same piece again for Fear.

evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. This special rule does not Push Cities. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g9jv, .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]
